stages.title: Orbital planning
stages.text: A first route from NASA orbital data. Large slopes and the rockfall zone are visible; small hazards are not.

stages.title: Rover reconnaissance
stages.text: In the sols before the walk, the rover drives the crew-rover route out and checks the walking paths. It finds soft ground the orbit could not see and the drive is replanned.

stages.title: Drone inspection
stages.text: The simulated drone perches on the pit floor facing the tallest part of the ice cliff (about 70 m), which the crew cannot reach on this EVA, and images the face and rockfall zone.

stages.title: Astronaut mission review
stages.text: Review the proposed trip: two astronauts drive the crew rover 2.3 km to a parking point on the plain, then walk about 730 m around the cliffs to a viewpoint facing a bluish, ice-consistent cliff face. None of this is crew clearance.

stats.Travel time: 129 min round trip + 20 min at the site
stats.Walkback: 117 min on foot if the crew rover fails; 238 of 240 min EVA
stats.View: Bluish cliff 44 m tall here, viewpoint 229 m from its foot (rockfall zone 85 m)
stats.Route status: Needs inspection: budgets fit, but the crew-rover drive is not yet modeled

orbital: Plan unverified: small hazards are below orbital resolution
rover: Rover stopped: wheel slip 38 percent, requesting input
drone: Simulated drone concept: rockfall zone suspected, not verified

sensor_evidence.thermal: simulated thermal camera: surface cooler than surroundings (possible loose material)

options.label: Reroute around the area
